heroHeadline: Taliban Surrounds Kabul's Shia High Council Office as Pakistan Kills 11 Militants in Balochistan IBOs
heroSubtitle: September 9, 2026 is Day 9,103 since the US launched Operation Enduring Freedom and Day 197 of Pakistan's Operation Ghazab lil-Haq. Taliban forces surrounded the office of Afghanistan's Shia High Council in Kabul's Karte Char area on September 8 without publicly disclosing a reason, extending a week-long crackdown on Shia institutions that began September 5 with the siege of the Khatam al-Nabieen seminary — where 28 students and teachers were forcibly evicted and detained (24 remain held) after three prominent Shia leaders were separately detained September 6, bringing the total detained to roughly 36. Separately, Pakistan's ISPR reported September 9 that security forces killed 11 Fitna al-Hindustan militants in intelligence-based operations in Kharan (8, September 6) and Washuk (3, September 7), Balochistan, seizing 2.9 tonnes of explosives allegedly intended for IEDs. The crackdown follows a bloody stretch of Pakistani counter-insurgency operations: ISPR says security forces killed 21 Fitna al-Khawarij militants across North Waziristan, Kohat and Dera Ismail Khan between September 3-5, part of a 72-hour, 48-militant Balochistan sweep through September 4. No formal ceasefire or new Urumqi round has been confirmed.
